subject: Recap + Playbook: Reserved infra & isolation requirements for HomeCareAI

Subject: Recap + Playbook: Reserved infra & isolation requirements for HomeCareAI

Hi Erin (and Peter),

Thanks again for taking time today — great conversation. Per our call, I wanted to capture: the key pain, your short- and medium-term goals, and a concrete recommended starting playbook for reserved capacity + isolation. Please flag anything I misremembered.

Summary of pain points (what you told us)
- Unpredictable inference cost spikes during scheduling windows (evening peak 6–9pm PT).
- Need strict tenant isolation for PHI-derived models and audit trails for SOC2/PCI review.
- Current infra setup has ~200ms p95 token latency under load; goal is to get that <120ms for interactive caregiver assistant.

Goals / success criteria
- Stable per-token cost within +/- 12% month-to-month for production traffic.
- SLO: p95 inference latency < 120ms for standard 1–2k token prompts; < 150ms for long prompts (3–5k).
- Isolation: dedicated GPU pool for PHI models with customer-managed VPC peering + KMS integration.
- Autoscale: ability to add 1–2 GPUs as burst capacity during 30–90 minute peaks.

Proposed starting playbook (our recommendation)
1) Reserved pool: start with a 3-GPU reserved pool (2x A100-class + 1x A30-class for batch/embeddings).
   - Rationale: gives headroom for concurrency and allows cost-optimized routing of smaller jobs to the A30.
2) Isolation: dedicated pool isolated in your VPC with KMS/HSM for key management and audit logging enabled.
3) Burst & autoscale policy: primary pool at fixed capacity; set burst policy to allow +2 GPUs for up to 2 hours/day with automatic fallback to a lower-cost open model if capacity constrained.
4) SLA targets: 99.9% availability on the dedicated pool; latency SLOs as above.

Immediate next steps (action items)
- Erin/Peter: confirm procurement timeline (target week for PO) and whether MSA redlines will be required.
- Marissa (cc): will prepare a pricing worksheet with a 12 and 24 month reserved commitment option.
- Dylan (cc): will draft an isolation runbook and audit log sample for your compliance team.
- Jonas: schedule a 30-minute technical review to validate exact model sizing and expected concurrency (I’ve proposed Thu 5/20 at 10am PT below).

Attachments: HomeCareAI_Estimate_v1.xlsx (costs by commitment length). Also including an initial MOP outline as a PDF.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the tech review.

Best,

Hi Erin / Peter — quick follow on the technical bits Erin asked about.

Per-model audit trails: Redwood captures structured request metadata (model id, caller token, request timestamp, request hash) and can emit logs to your SIEM via secure forwarders. We’ll attach a sample audit log schema (see MOP_dedicated-pool.pdf). If you need payload-level retention off by default for privacy, we can provide hashed payloads only and include an allowlist for debugging windows.

Sizing / latency: based on the model family you described (7B instruction-tuned conversational model) and the concurrency estimate (~18 qps with 1–2k avg tokens), our internal bench suggests:
- 2x A100-class GPUs for low-latency serving (primary pool) + 1x A30 for background batch/embeddings.
- With continuous batching and KV-cache priming, p95 < 120ms is achievable for 1–2k prompts at ~18 concurrent interactive sessions provided model is quantized to int8 and we pin instances to the dedicated pool.

Autoscale policy options (pick one):
A) Fixed reserved (3 GPUs) + burst pool (+2 GPUs) for scheduled peak windows (cost-predictable).
B) Reserved (2 GPUs) + dynamic autoscale up to +4 GPUs using warm-standby nodes (higher capex/toe in cost).

I recommend A for your initial rollout to keep costs and predictability aligned with your SLOs.

Onboarding ops contacts: assign an infra lead who can accept VPC peering invites and KMS provisioning (I’ll include a short checklist in the runbook).

I attached the initial MOP that outlines audit log schema and a short onboarding checklist.

Cheers,

Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
